inputs.resume_text:
Rahul Deshpande
PGP 2026-27 (one-year MBA), Indian School of Business, Hyderabad

EDUCATION
PGP, Indian School of Business, 2026-27
B.E., Computer Engineering, Pune Institute of Computer Technology, 2018, 74%
CFA Level II candidate

WORK EXPERIENCE (7 years)
HDFC Bank, Mumbai | Senior Manager, Credit Risk - Mid-Market Corporates | Apr 2022 - Mar 2026
- Underwrote and monitored a portfolio of 85 mid-market borrowers with exposure of INR 2,400 crore
- Led the credit review of a stressed auto-components borrower; restructured INR 140 crore of exposure and avoided an NPA classification
- Built an early-warning dashboard on GST and bank-statement data, flagging 11 accounts 2 quarters before rating downgrades
- Managed a team of 3 credit analysts
Axis Bank | Credit Analyst | Jul 2018 - Mar 2022
- Prepared credit appraisal notes for 60+ SME loan proposals

ACTIVITIES
- Mentor, Finance Club, ISB
- Ran a half marathon (Mumbai Marathon, 2024)
inputs.jd_text:
Manager - Corporate Finance (FP&A and Capital Allocation)
Varuna Industries Ltd, Pune

Varuna Industries is a listed auto-components manufacturer (revenue INR 6,500 crore) with 14 plants in India.

Role
- Own the annual operating plan and monthly business reviews for two business units
- Evaluate capex proposals (new lines, capacity expansion) and present recommendations to the CFO
- Work with treasury on working-capital and debt decisions
- Lead a team of 2 analysts

Must have
- 5+ years in corporate finance, credit or investment banking
- Strong financial modelling and capital-budgeting skills
- Stakeholder management with plant and business heads

plan.warmup_question: What finance skill have you picked up recently, and where has it been useful?
plan.background_question: Walk me through your career from Axis Bank through HDFC Bank to your current MBA, focusing on the choices along the way.

slots.core_question: I see you led the review of a stressed auto-components borrower at HDFC Bank. What drove the restructuring decision?
slots.intent_private: Needs the borrower context, Rahul’s own credit analysis, the alternatives he weighed, and how the INR 140 crore restructuring affected risk and the NPA outcome.
likely_probes: Which part of the analysis was yours?
What option did you reject?
What was the exposure amount you restructured?

slots.core_question: How did the early-warning dashboard at HDFC Bank come about?
slots.intent_private: Needs the warning problem, how Rahul selected and combined GST and bank-statement signals, and how he validated that the 11 flagged accounts preceded rating downgrades.
likely_probes: What did you build first?
Why did you choose those data signals?
How many accounts did the dashboard flag?

slots.core_question: What did you have to figure out first as a Finance Club mentor at ISB?
slots.intent_private: Needs a specific mentoring situation, Rahul’s personal contribution, and a concrete change in the student’s preparation or performance.
likely_probes: What was your role in that situation?
What did you do first?
What changed for the student afterward?

slots.core_question: What is pulling you from banking credit risk toward corporate finance and capital allocation?
slots.intent_private: Needs a specific reason for the move grounded in Rahul’s credit-risk experience, plus evidence that he understands the target role’s FP&A, capex and business-stakeholder demands.
likely_probes: Which part of your HDFC experience prompted that direction?
What have you done during the MBA to prepare for this move?
Which responsibility in this role attracts you most?

plan.plan_notes: The plan prioritizes Rahul’s strongest, most relevant HDFC claims and includes the Finance Club activity because this is a back-your-resume interview. His credit-risk background is adjacent to the corporate-finance role, but the move toward FP&A and capital allocation should be explored neutrally; direct evidence of financial modelling, capex evaluation and plant-facing stakeholder management is limited.
